Seal Pupping Season Begins: The annual seal pupping season has officially begun along the Larris coastline, with early sightings reported near the eastern cliffs and the edge of the moors.
Residents are reminded not to approach the colony. Disturbing the animals can result in injury or fines.
Binoculars are available for public use at the harbor office. One pair has gone missing already.
Organ Out of Order: Fr. Jean-Noël has announced that the organ at St. Dymphne's has gone silent. As of this Sunday, services are being held without music until further notice.
It always sounded a little haunted, but everyone agrees - that's what made it ours.
A donation jar for repairs now sits between the donation box (the old one) and the statue of Our Lady.

Minor Delay in Postal Deliveries: Postal service will be slightly delayed this week due to a misadventure involving our dedicated postman, a muddy hill and his usual luck.
Deliveries will resume shortly, in the meantime, mail may be collected at the post office during regular hours.
Tired of Small-Town Tides?: Villebourg Fisheries Ltd. is recruiting seasonal crew for city trawlers. Shifts last two weeks at sea, with pay on return. Apply at the harbor office before Thursday.
Hatches, Matches, and Despatches: Viviane M. died early Monday morning, her heart giving out without much warning. Lately, she'd been saying she couldn't sleep. Well. Goodnight, sweetheart.
Last Call for Ice Cream: As usual, the pier's ice cream truck will switch to hot soup service on October 1st. Spoons deposit scheme remains the same.

Letters to the Editor:
Trail Markers
To whoever keeps turning moor trail markers into fairy rings, please stop. Tourists have started getting stuck in the bog again.

Re: Visiting Hours Change
Not everyone can get off work by six, especially out-of-towners like us from the city. It's our hospital too, even if it's on your side of the road.

Cave canem
I wish to report that my interaction with the newly appointed medical staff member, identifiable by red hair pigmentation, created an atmosphere of interpersonal discomfort. Condolences to the nuns in prolonged proximity.

SPECIAL WORDOKU OFFER!: Exclusively from the corner of Fire Brigade St and Pyromaniacs Blvd!...

Urban Seal Activity Continues: The lone seal spotted near the soup truck this Friday has not returned to the colony. Instead, it has made its way through town, visiting alleys, docks, and briefly settling among the lily beds outside St. Dymphne's.
Reactions vary: some say it's a blessing, others worry about disease or bad omens.
A group of children were seen attempting to "guard" the seal near the loading dock on Saturday afternoon, using cardboard signs and a stolen traffic cone. No injuries were reported.

Foragers Personals: F, 30. New to foraging scene. Into heather, curious about bog myrtle. Looking for someone taller than a juniper bush with strong basket game.
M, 55. Experienced mushroom hunter looking for passionate companion for long crawls through the mist, berry-picking at dawn... and perhaps life.
Couple, retired, both mid-60s. Our children don't visit, so we seek a third for sphagnum gathering. We enjoy long afternoons knee-deep in moss, and are open to trying new techniques.
Communion Wafers Update: The sisters at St. Dymphne's have confirmed that starting next Sunday, communion will feature the return of their popular pumpkin spice wafers.
Available while the leaves fall and no one from the diocese is watching.

Which Liturgical Object Are You?: The much-anticipated return of Father Jean-Noël's column! In this edition, you will finally identify the sacred tool of the Mass that has been lurking inside your soul ever since your first baptismal splash!
Letters to the Editor:
Re: Organ Out of Order
When I was a young boy, my father talked Father Jean-Noël into letting me "practise" on the organ after school. It terrified me, and I'm fairly sure I returned the favour, hammering at it until I learned what I was actually doing.
But once I played Fisher's Paradise, the altar boys burst out laughing, and suddenly I wasn't alone anymore. So if I knocked a few years off its life back then, sorry, old friend. And thank you.

Re: Cave canem (1)
We Sisters have no complaints. Do not mistake, dear correspondent, a guarded manner for cruelty, for one may be reserved in speech yet faithful in duty, and that is no sin...
...Remember also: such hearts often wear brave faces, hiding their pain in silence. Speak kindly, that no soul be burdened.

Dear seal,
My son said this is classic illusory correlation reinforced by suggestibility and expectancy effects. My neighbour said her ankle stopped hurting after she walked around you three times.
...I'm not telling my son, but the migraine I'd had for days was gone by evening too.

Re: Cave canem (2)
Dear observer, if your courage were equal to your words, you might direct future observations to my face rather than to this column.
* Initial submission revised due to foul language and excessive hostility.

Town Seal Triggers Child Protest: Despite dropping temperatures and growing concern from adults, a group of children identifying themselves as a "pod" continues to assemble near the seal's preferred resting areas.
Activities observed include silence, stillness, mild territorial behaviour, and the consumption of impressive quantities of fish.
Schools have noted increased truancy, while parents report resistance to routine, including meals, homework, and bedtime. Minor illness is circulating, as expected.
No official demands have been issued. No end date announced. The seal, for its part, appears unbothered and very much at home.

Friday Music at Expresso:
Live music returns to Expresso coffee bar this Friday evening! The programme begins at 8:30, featuring a visiting singer accompanied by saxophone. Keys may join if our resident decides to show up this time.
(We know you read this.)
Expect good company, dimmed light, and music that makes talking easier. Admission free, drinks and cakes as usual.
Outer Seals Voyages: Daily trips to the sandbank beyond the bay where the wild seals spend their days. For those who have already waved at the friendly one in town and wish to meet the more introverted rest.
7 seats per trip, no judgement of passengers. Find us at Pier R.
Hatches, Matches, and Despatches: Some readers may recall the match made through the Foragers Personals last autumn, and the editors are pleased to report that their union will be made official this week, in the moors themselves.
Guests can reach the site by following the telegraph line until the last pole before the land turns uncertain. Local seals, of course, are considered invited.
The Lord clearly moves in mysterious ecosystems.
Tired of Small-Town Tides?: Villebourg Fisheries Ltd. is recruiting seasonal crew for city trawlers. Shifts last two weeks at sea, with pay on return. Apply at the harbor office before Sunday.
